device: Physical Quest 3, Vulkan, saved Mobile quality, 72 Hz. The headset was on its stand.
conditions: The separately named local development fixture used Meta’s Rec Room fixture, a fixed 8 × 8 glass board at 60 cm and scripted body positions. The camera looked 37 degrees down from 1.58 m. The gameplay engine, glass shaders, six landings and native OVR compositor actually ran on the headset. The fixture muted game audio during the timed workload. Physical room fitting, head motion and comfort need a wearer.
timing: Unity frame rate is total gameplay frames divided by measured Unity window time. Draw calls and triangles are the maxima from those windows. Native OVR samples are summarized per matching package launch. Their one-second clock starts at its own session origin, so they are not attributed to individual Unity frames. A graphics result requires positive Unity draw calls and triangles and native Meta samples with a submitted, nonzero-size eye buffer. Off-head simulation that kept ticking at 72 Hz while drawing nothing is excluded.
offHeadLimits: Ordinary launches submitted stereo frames for a short interval. A case lists its observed duration and only records an ending-to-Results time when the fixture actually reached Results. The first keep-awake attempt reached the Quest boundary dialog and provided no gameplay frames. The timed proximity override and Meta CSV setting were restored. The measured launches used ordinary proximity behavior.

waterSplashPlacementTrial.change: The separate fixture optionally instantiated the approved Meta Floor Zone splash and deactivated it before the fall. Baseline instantiated the same asset at impact. No shipped source or APK was modified by this experiment.
waterSplashPlacementTrial.measurement: An impact window is the approximately one-second Unity aggregation containing the expected Water contact, 0.40 s plus sqrt(160 / 9.8) after the loss marker. The following window is reported separately. Whole-fall and contact-window maxima measure frame intervals, not GPU work for a particular effect. Normal-2 also had a standard Perfetto capture.

perfetto.tool: Meta Horizon Developer Tools, standard Perfetto capture and local trace_processor_shell, process com.wa003.floorfracture.renderbench.
perfetto.timing: Quest game event markers and Unity windows share Android elapsed time since boot. Values are relative to the event marker or expected contact. The selected comparison window covers 150 ms before and 300 ms after.

maximum-shatter.event: First actual 32-pane shatter marked by the game CSV on the Android boot clock.

water-contact.event: Expected Water contact from the fall marker, 0.40 s hold and 80 m at 9.8 m/s². The Unity marker has millisecond precision.

maximum-contact.event: First actual 32-pane shatter marked by the game CSV on the Android boot clock.

reproductionInputs.storedInputs: Base and comfort fixture patches against the game revision, reference to the installed MRUK Rec Room, and measurement replay instructions. No user room data.

comfortAndAndroidQuit.method: On physical Quest the isolated fixture requests natural Reduced, a fresh start and a Full Skip per theme, then calls the game's actual Android Quit. It tries the Results buttons and records if the off-head tracking guard requires invoking their game handlers directly. Both controller rays and both fingertip pokes were independently exercised in the native simulator. A wearer still needs to test the actual input and comfort.
comfortAndAndroidQuit.timing: The fixture supplied Reduced directly to the game without persisting a preference; the raw reduced_motion CSV field still reflects the default saved preference. The recorded fall and reduced-results markers bracket the measured windows. The 3.9-second natural timeline is distinct from the 9.45-second Full timing, and the second fall starts after the reset. Only intervals with rendered geometry and samples with nonzero compositor eye buffers are counted.
